question: Who founded the English newspaper 'Mahratta'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bal Gangadhar Tilak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak, often referred to as the "Father of Indian Unrest," was a prominent freedom fighter in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He founded the English newspaper 'Mahratta' along with the Marathi newspaper 'Kesari' to awaken political consciousness among Indians.
 
• Tilak was one of the first leaders to advocate for Swaraj (self-rule) and was a key member of the Indian National Congress.
 
• His famous slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it" inspired many Indians to join the freedom struggle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**

 
 
• Born on July 23, 1856, in Ratnagiri, Maharashtra, Tilak was a scholar, mathematician, philosopher, and ardent nationalist.
 
• He played a significant role in the Home Rule Movement and was a vocal advocate of radical nationalism in India.
 
• Tilak's works such as 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' and 'Gita Rahasya' reflect his deep understanding of Indian culture and philosophy.
 
• He was imprisoned several times by the British for his revolutionary activities, and his efforts greatly contributed to the independence movement.
 
 
 
• **Mahratta and Kesari**
 
 
• 'Mahratta' was an English weekly newspaper, and 'Kesari' was a Marathi newspaper started by Tilak in 1881.
 
• Both newspapers aimed at educating the Indian public about political issues and mobilizing them against British rule.
 
• They were instrumental in spreading Tilak's revolutionary ideas and garnering support for the freedom struggle.
 
• These publications faced censorship and suppression by the British government, but they continued to play a pivotal role in the nationalist movement.
